coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 7 days out with a 92/100 recovery score and RHR of 56—you're primed. Run an easy 5–7 miles at Z2 (140–150 bpm based on your recent avg of 128–129 on harder efforts) on rolling terrain with 300–400 ft of vert. This is a shakeout: keep it conversational, test your legs for any niggles, and dial in race-day nutrition strategy on the trail. Friday before a Saturday long run in taper is about confidence, not volume. You're down 15 miles from last week already—don't creep back up.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your 8.3h sleep at 88.8% efficiency is excellent—leverage it by front-loading carbs today. Aim for 6–7g per kg of body weight carbohydrate across the day (adjust for your weight; assume ~140g if 60kg, ~180g if 75kg). On today's shakeout, consume 30–40g carbs per hour (sports drink, gels, or real food) to rehearse your race-day gut tolerance. Tomorrow's long run will demand similar intake; test it now when stakes are low. Hydrate to pale urine; you'll be at altitude in a week.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your limiting factor in taper, not training. You've banked 8.3h last night—maintain that. Aim for 8–9h tonight; if travel or work stress creeps in, prioritize blackout conditions and a consistent bedtime. RHR at 56 (down from your 30-day avg of 64.7) signals parasympathetic dominance; protect it. Skip ice baths or aggressive massage today—gentle movement, foam roll the feet and shins for 5 min, and call it done. You're not recovering *from* much anymore; you're preserving freshness.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: One week to race. The hard work is done; your peak phase loaded the fitness. Today's shakeout and tomorrow's long run are about anchoring confidence, not adding fitness. The Julian Alps demand alpine pacing discipline and aid-station discipline—neither comes from panic. Use today's run to rehearse your race fueling, test your legs on real vert, and mentally rehearse the descent strategy on a technical section. You're not overtrained; you're tapered. Trust it.
